items.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: His name was Earl Evans. He was a tech sergeant.

ctx.x: No I didn’t really play bass. And he says, “yeah, go ahead and try it.” His name was Earl Evans. He was a tech sergeant. He was somewhere, what’s that, Nebraska or someplace now. And he says, “go ahead, try it.” So I picked it up. He says, “you want to try it for a few days? I says, “yeah.” So I took it up and I learned how to tune G D A and E, and because of my tuba experience I would play root and fifth, I learned what root and fifth were, the finger here and the finger there you know, that type of thing. So I…
Did you have to be in uniform when you’d go into town like that?
